data.title: Bab el-Mandeb strait, Yemenis flee as migrants arrive
data.content:
## Busier than ever before the escalation

Neither the regional war nor the earlier blockade announcement slowed migration to Yemen. Between January and August 2026, IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix recorded 122,258 arrivals from the Horn of Africa in Yemen. In eight months, the route has already passed the long-term annual average and the total for all of 2025. In June, IOM linked higher arrivals in Abyan to the suspension of security campaigns against smuggling networks. [...] This is what polycrisis looks like on the ground. As we argue in the Mixed Migration Review 2026, polycrisis is not a backdrop but a mechanism. A war between states impacts local conflict, which changed who controls a strait, which pushed people across a sea into a country whose response capacity had already been hollowed out by aid cuts. Each crisis makes the others harder to manage. [...] Figures for September are not yet available at the time of writing. Most boats from Djibouti land on the Gulf of Aden coast, in Lahj and Abyan, rather than on the Red Sea coast where the fighting took place. It is therefore too early to say whether the escalation will reduce crossings, shift landing points, or change little. The experience of 2015 and 2016 suggests the last option should not be ruled out.
